20.21.7.en: * "When he reckons himself satisfied, he falls into anxiety" [22 LXX]. This means that fruit rots when it ripens. But as we have said many times, what Job's friends said was not to abase the wicked and the ungodly, but rather to shake Job's patience.

20.21.8.en: And since the wrestler bore the sorrows that had come upon him with a great soul, confident in the benefits that patience brings, he (Zophar) threatened him that the future would be worse than the past.

20.21.9.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem *Truly, a man's life does not consist in his possessions, through the abundance he has; rather, he is counted blessed and possessed of a glorious hope who is rich toward God.

20.21.10.en: St. Cyril of Alexandria * When we gain a farthing we are filled with joy, and when we lose half a farthing we sink into sorrow.

20.22.0.en: St. Jerome When he is about to fill his belly, God shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him, and shall rain it upon him while he is eating [23].

20.22.1.en: Nothing stirs up the fury of God's wrath against a man like his wronging his brother. While he thinks that he is filling his belly by wronging his brother, the fury of divine wrath rains fire and brimstone upon him. "Upon the wicked he shall rain... fire and brimstone" (Ps 11:6).

20.22.2.en: It takes him by surprise in the moments of his enjoyment of feasts, as he takes his food. Perhaps Zophar is pointing here to the death of Job's sons and daughters while a feast was being held.

20.22.3.en: He also points here to what happened in the days of the Flood, and to the destruction that came upon Sodom and Gomorrah, as the Lord Christ says: "They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all. Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot; they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded; but the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all" (Lk 17:27-29).

20.22.4.en: * [To fill his belly, so that God casts his wrath upon him, and rains his war upon him] [23]... [The rain of God's war] is the striking of hearts that exalt themselves against Him, and the wounding of the hateful soul with the arrows of His judgment... Whereas it would have been fitting for (the covetous man) to remind himself how he coveted what was not his, and with a greater evil set it in himself to gather the things he desired. And at another time he will grieve that he will be parted from the things he gathered.

20.22.6.en: He shall flee from the iron weapon,

20.23.0.en: and the bow of steel shall strike him through [24].

20.23.1.en: Their destruction will be certain, without any possibility of escaping it. "He shall flee from the iron weapon." Fleeing points to iniquity, for the wicked man does not think of confessing his sins in humility before God to be reconciled with Him, but all he thinks of is escaping the vengeance that pursues him, yet in vain. For if he escapes the sword, "the bow of steel shall strike him through," or a bow of tempered steel. It is as though God uses the sword for those who think that they fight against Him by their own strength, and the bow for those who think that they are able to flee from Him by their cunning. For whoever thinks that he is able to escape one punishment finds another punishment pursuing him.

20.23.2.en: * This means that He (God) will overwhelm him with sufferings... But what are these sufferings? Let us pay attention. "Let him flee by any means from the power of the sword, and let the bow of bronze wound him. And let the arrow pierce his body, let the stars be against his dwelling, and let terrors come upon him" [24-25 LXX]. Job did not fall under these blows, for God forbade the Accuser (Satan) to kill him; therefore neither iron nor bronze nor any spear could approach him from among Satan's hired soldiers. Even as much as they brought upon him... no fire was kindled against him, that is, the fire whose source is not the earth. For Satan has no authority to stir up the terror of the heavens against him.

20.23.3.en: Zophar threatened Job with these things, wishing to terrify the wrestler with fear on every side. As for Job, he did not say how or from where these things come upon him, for he was confident in his righteousness.

20.23.4.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * [He will flee from iron weapons, and rush toward the bow of bronze] [24]. We must know that covetousness sometimes creeps in upon people through pride, and sometimes through fear. Therefore some aim at appearing with greater authority, and burn to obtain what belongs to others. Likewise there are people who fear lest they come to be in need of the necessities of life, and so give over their minds to covetousness to seek what belongs to others, imagining that what they have does not suffice them. Now, the expression "iron" is suited to all "necessities." For it troubles the life of the needy with wounds of sorrow. It is an expression of the need for necessities, which leads to a painful life... [The iron entered into his soul] (Ps 105:18). What then are the iron weapons but the necessities of the present life that press upon the life of the needy with harshness? Iron is destroyed by rust, but bronze is destroyed by it with greater difficulty. Therefore iron signifies the present, temporary necessities, while bronze signifies the eternal destiny.

20.23.6.en: * Do you wish to build your city well? [A little with the fear of the Lord is better than a great treasure without the fear] (cf. Prov 15:16). A man's wealth must work for the salvation of his soul, not its destruction. Wealth is for salvation if one uses it well, and thus it is a snare if one does not know how to use it (Prov 13:8). For what profit is a man's money if it does not support him on his journey?

20.23.7.en: St. Ambrose It is drawn, and cometh out of the body; yea, the glittering sword cometh out of his gall:

20.24.1.en: The destruction will be complete when the bow pierces him and comes out of his gall, and terrors and very violent dread come upon him, and the pains of his death are exceedingly painful. Thus death falls upon the wicked man, pouncing on him and making him taste bitterness.

20.24.2.en: * [The terrifying ones come and fall upon him] [25]. Who are those here called the terrifying ones but the evil spirits, whom pious minds must fear and avoid? It is thought that these same evil spirits each cling to particular vices. When this wicked man leaves one group of faults for a moment and begins to commit another group, then surely [the terrifying ones come and fall upon him], so that when the soul of the wicked leaves one group of evil habits, another group takes it captive. Often you see a wicked man with earthly authority stirred by tumultuous passions, and he carries out all that his anger suggests to him. And when his anger subsides, lust stirs his soul. And when lust ceases for a time, self-importance at once occupies his heart on the ground that he is violent, and in order to show others that he is fearsome he aims at making himself an object of dread... Thus it is truly said of him whose mind's vice seizes the place of another vice: "The terrifying ones come and fall upon him."

20.24.4.en: All darkness shall be hid in his secret places:

20.24.5.en: a fire not blown shall consume him;

20.25.0.en: it shall go ill with him that is left in his tabernacle [26].

20.25.1.en: The darkness in which the wicked man wraps himself is hidden; it is a thick darkness that not a single ray of light pierces. An inward darkness that passes through to him where he thinks he is safe, hidden in a place no one can reach. Perhaps by the hiding place he means his conscience, for the wicked man suffers from the darkness that falls in his depths, to find himself in gloom and bewilderment, from which none can save him except his returning in repentance to the true light, the Giver of peace.

20.25.2.en: A destroying fire that has not been blown is kindled within him, that is, no sound of it is heard. All see the wicked man's ruin and burning without being able to know the cause. Just as Jonah saw the gourd withered, but did not see the worm that caused it to wither (Jon 4:7).

20.25.3.en: And by his saying [a fire not blown] he indicates that the destroying fire of sin has fuel that burns very quickly and needs no blowing. "All the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up" (Mal 4:1).

20.25.4.en: "It feeds on the remnant in his tent": his evil creeps into his tent, or into his family, and becomes a cause of the destruction of many of his household.

20.25.5.en: * "All darkness is hidden in his secret places" [26]... It is said that all "darkness is hidden in his secret places," because he does not display all the evils that are in him, but he must bring them all down upon his fellow creatures.

20.25.6.en: [A fire not kindled shall consume him]; these few words declare the fire of Gehenna in a most astonishing manner. For material fire, in order to be fire, needs material fuel. And to continue, it must be supplied with the wood that is heaped upon it, as we know. It does not exist unless it is kindled, and does not continue unless it is served with fuel. Contrary to this, the fire of Gehenna, while it is a fire that destroys the sons of perdition who are cast into it bodily, is not kindled by human effort, nor does it continue by wood being cast into it. But once it exists, it remains unquenchable, and needs no kindling, and its heat does not diminish... The justice of the Almighty, since it foreknew the coming events, created from the beginning of the world the fire of Gehenna, which was to begin for the punishment of the wicked, and its heat will never cease, and it needs no fuel...

20.25.7.en: It was said by the Psalmist: [Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven in the time of thine anger: the LORD shall swallow them up in his wrath, and the fire shall devour them] (Ps 21:9). Thus Holy Scripture shows that the lost are burned inwardly and outwardly. It testifies that they are devoured by fire, and at the same time become a fiery furnace; so by fire they are tormented in the body, and by sorrow they burn in the spirit.

20.25.8.en: [Being left in his tent, it will be with him in the trial], for since he placed all delight in bodily life [he dwells in the tent of the body].

20.25.10.en: * Why did (Satan) not enter the blessed Peter, James and John, or any of the rest of the apostles?

20.25.11.en: Why did he enter Judas Iscariot?

20.25.12.en: What did Satan find in him?

20.25.13.en: Satan could not approach any of those we have mentioned, because their hearts were upright and their love for Christ steadfast. In the betrayer there was room for Satan. The malignant disease, covetousness, which the blessed Paul said is the root of all evils (1 Tim 6:10), had gained mastery over him. Satan is cunning in doing evil. When he gains possession of a person's soul, he does not fight him with a common vice, but rather seeks for the person he has mastered a means by which to make him his prey.

20.25.14.en: St. Cyril the Great * Three men came to Abraham (Gen 18:1-2) in the heat of the day; but in the case of Sodom two angels came in the evening (Gen 19:1). Good things are likened to light, and evil things to evening, until the Sun of righteousness shall arise upon them (Mal 4:2). For the punishment of the wicked is night and darkness, but the righteous shall shine as the light (Prov 4:18; Mt 13:43).

20.25.15.en: Fr. Theodore, Bishop of Mopsuestia * To the others He said: "Depart from me, ye cursed" (Mt 25:41). He did not say that they are cursed by the Father, for the Father did not cast the curse upon them, but their own works do that. He did not say that the eternal fire is prepared for them alone, but "for the devil and his angels." For concerning the Kingdom, indeed, when He said: "Come... inherit the kingdom," He added, prepared for you from the foundation of the world (Mt 25:34). But concerning the fire He did not say this, but "prepared for the devil." I prepared the Kingdom for you, but the fire I did not prepare for you but for the devil and his angels; yet you cast yourselves into it. You have attributed it to yourselves.

20.26.0.en: St. John Chrysostom The heaven shall reveal his iniquity; and the earth shall rise up against him [27].

20.26.1.en: The God of heaven, who sees hidden things, declares the evils of the wicked who persist in their evil, and the earth uncovers their iniquities and takes vengeance on them. [The earth shall disclose her blood] (Isa 26:21). For heaven cannot endure iniquity, and the earth rises up against it, and the wicked find no place for themselves here or there, but settle in Gehenna.

20.26.2.en: * "The heavens reveal his iniquity, and the earth rises up against him" [27]. What do we understand by the heavens but the righteous, and by the earth the sinners? So in the Lord's Prayer it is prayed: [Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven], to mean that the will of our Creator, as it is fulfilled in the righteous, may it be fulfilled in all sinners also. Moreover it is said of the righteous: [The heavens declare the glory of God] (Ps 19:1). And to man, when he sinned, the sentence was declared: [Dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return]. And so when the wicked man is dragged to the dreadful judgment, it is said: "The heavens reveal his iniquity, and the earth rises up against him," for the man who here had no pity on the good or the wicked, at his dreadful interrogation, the life of the righteous and of sinners bears witness against him...

20.26.3.en: But it is also possible that "the earth" signifies not the sinful, condemned life, but those who are occupied with earthly matters, and through almsgiving and with tears obtain eternal life. Of these the Psalmist speaks when it was announced that the Lord is coming for judgment: "He shall call to the heavens from above, and to the earth, that he may judge his people" (Ps 50:4). For He calls the heavens from above, when those leave all that they have and hold fast to the inclination toward the heavenly life, they are called to sit with Him in judgment, and to come with Him as judges...

20.26.4.en: Nothing that the wicked man has done will be hidden from the insight of the time of judgment, though truly many deeds are now hidden, through deceit, from his fellow creatures; in the day of judgment they will appear in the light.

20.26.6.en: If the heavens declare the iniquity of the wicked, and the earth exposes and opposes him, then it is fitting for the Church to ask the faithful to flee from the wicked who are determined on evil, and not from sinners who need someone to witness before them to the Gospel of forgiveness.

20.26.7.en: St. Cyprian emphasizes not only the severe divine punishments that come upon the wicked who oppose the truth, but also demands that God's children separate themselves from them so that God's wrath may not come upon them. [We find this plainly in the Book of Numbers, when Korah, Dathan and Abiram claimed the right to offer sacrifices in opposition to Aaron the priest. For the Lord teaches through Moses that the people are bound to separate from them lest they be joined to the same iniquity of the guilty and defile themselves with the same crime. "And he spake unto the congregation, saying, Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest ye be consumed in all their sins" (Num 16:26).]

20.26.8.en: * Do what you can to remove the wicked person, for as soon as he goes out Christ will dwell in you.

20.26.9.en: Origen * You despise gold; another loves it.

20.26.10.en: You scorn wealth; he runs after it with eagerness.

20.26.11.en: You love quietness, weakness and a hidden, private life, but he finds pleasure in speaking shamelessly in public squares, as in the streets and public places...

20.26.12.en: Do not be under one roof with him. Do not rely on your former chastity. You are no holier than David nor wiser than Solomon... If in your priestly work you are obliged to visit a widow or a virgin, do not enter the house alone. Do not let your companions think lightly of you... Do not sit alone with a woman in secret without a witness with you. If she wishes to disclose some private and secret matter, she has a nurse or a housekeeper or a virgin or a maiden or a wife. She cannot be without friends other than you, so that she must pour out her private secrets to you.

20.27.0.en: St. Jerome The increase of his house shall depart, and his goods shall flow away in the day of his wrath [28].

20.27.1.en: His offspring, which is the increase of his house, will be uprooted, as death comes upon them untimely, or they are forced to flee from their land and so are scattered and uprooted.

20.27.2.en: As wealth flows to the wicked man swiftly through injustice and deceit, so it is also dissipated with the same swiftness when divine wrath comes upon him.

20.27.3.en: * When the wrath of the Judge is declared, (the wicked man) is handed over to the fires of wrath, and is removed from the sight of (the Judge). For he who in life would not raise his mind to the heavenly things, since his sins drag him downward, will fall from before the face of the Judge into the depths of punishment. Now the Judge sees and bears with the sinner in his sins, because it is the day of gentleness, not the day of wrath, for He waits expectantly for everyone's conversion. Now is the day of gentleness, and while the hypocrite remains motionless, not stirred, practicing many evils and not disciplined by scourges, he will be driven out on the day of wrath, when he is carried to the punishment of vengeance; he is cut off from the face of the eternal Judge.

20.28.0.en: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed unto him by God [29].

20.28.1.en: What the wicked man gathers for himself is not the wealth he acquired for a time, but the wrath that comes upon him. This is his permanent portion, and his eternal inheritance in the fire of Gehenna.

20.28.2.en: This is Zophar's speech, and it carried something of the truth, but he was mistaken in thinking that all this must come upon every wicked man while he is in this world, and that whoever has affliction come upon him in this life, that is a sign of the evil of the one who has fallen under it.

20.28.3.en: Zophar gave a sound interpretation of the working of evil in the life of the wicked man, but he erred in applying this doctrine, and he did not present the thought purely, but it was tainted with an evil inclination toward Job and an attempt to affirm that he is a hypocrite.

20.28.4.en: Truly evil is terrifying and sin is exceedingly sinful, but it is not for us to judge and condemn others according to our human outlook.

20.28.5.en: * If, when he was in this life, he had been careful to act uprightly, his portion would have been fellowship with the Lord in the Kingdom of Heaven. But since he chose to submit to evil lusts, his portion from the Lord is to be found in torment, since he did not seek to obtain fellowship in the grace of this Lord...

20.28.6.en: Now the saints do not desire to obtain a portion from the Lord, but to obtain the Lord Himself as their portion. For this the prophet prays, saying: "God is my portion for ever" (Ps 73:26).

20.28.7.en: But the wicked man, since he did not strive for the Lord Himself to be his portion, finds fire his portion, not the Lord. And being removed from the face of God, because he did not seek to find joy in Him, he is tormented, being unworthy of God.

20.28.9.en: * Those who consent to iniquity will have no portion among the immortals.

20.28.10.en: St. Anthony the Great * Let us see next what God commands us to do, for He says: "Give glory to the LORD your God, before he cause darkness, and before your feet stumble upon the dark mountains, and, while ye look for light" (Jer 13:16). For He wants whoever gives the Lord glory to give Him glory while the light exists, because the glory of the Lord cannot be proclaimed when darkness comes. When then does darkness come, and when does it not? [Work while the light is in you](ح). For the light is in fact in you, as long as you carry within you the Lord Christ, who said of Himself: "I am the light of the world." And as long as this light is in you, give glory to the Lord; but know that darkness can come, so you must not wait for this darkness to fall, but give glory to the Lord before its coming.

20.28.11.en: * Perhaps we can clearly understand this matter if we use the words of the Lord Christ: [Work while it is day. Night comes when no one can work](ط); by day He means our present time, and by darkness and night, the end of the world and its passing away because of the punishment of the wicked. And Amos the prophet says: "Woe unto you that desire the day of the LORD! to what end is it for you? the day of the LORD is darkness, and not light" (Amos 5:18). If you know how great the sorrow and misery will be at the destruction of the world, grief will strike nearly most of the human race, who are punished for their sins, and then you will know that the atmosphere will become so dark and gloomy that no one will be able to glorify God, because even the righteous God has commanded, saying: [Go, my people, enter into your house, and shut your door upon you; hide for a little or for much, until the heat of my wrath is ended](ي).

20.28.12.en: * As what God has prepared for those who love Him surpasses the mind, so also the torments He has prepared for the wicked surpass the mind.

20.28.13.en: * Each one of us brings upon himself punishment for sin, the size of the punishment according to the kind and nature of the transgression... The debt collector comes to complete his work, and I resist him. I know that if I am not in debt at all, he has no authority over me. If I have a debt, the debt collector will send me to prison.

20.28.15.en: Your voice cuts through the flame of my evils!

20.28.17.en: Who can quench the flame of my evils, and who will pour the waters of Your righteousness within me, Your sweet voice!

20.28.18.en: * Since the fall of Adam we have learned that the tree of evil must be uprooted, that the tree of Your righteousness may be planted in us.

20.28.19.en: Let the temple of the devil with its abominations be uprooted, that by Your Holy Spirit You may establish in us Your holy temple.

20.28.20.en: Cut off, destroy and pull down what in me is not Yours, and plant and establish what is Yours, that I may become Your holy garden and Your holy temple.

20.28.21.en: * Pull down, O Lord, every strange leprous building, let its stones be taken down and cast out.

20.28.22.en: Let no defiled stone remain within me, for I am Your holy city.

20.28.23.en: Remove from my heart every thorn and plant in me Your garden, that I may become Your vineyard, exceedingly beloved to You.

20.28.24.en: I offer You of what is Yours, of the fruit of Your Holy Spirit.

20.28.25.en: That You may call Your heavenly friends, saying:

20.28.26.en: "Eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved" (Song 5:1).

20.28.27.en: Come, O Lord Jesus, and dwell in my depths, where Your joyful garden is, and the temple of Your holiness!

20.28.28.en: *I know that the enemy of good offers pleasures and delights, but they are full of poison.

20.28.29.en: The joys of the ruler of this world will not last!

20.28.30.en: The sufferings we receive with thanksgiving from Your hands are sweeter than all the delights of the world!

20.28.31.en: *My sins crush me! At times in pride I do not care what I do, and at others in discouragement, so that despair reigns over my whole being.

20.28.32.en: I know that my sins have created enmity with Your word and Your commandment.

20.28.33.en: But Your word in the sweetness of its love disciplines, not to destroy me, but to bring me back to You, that I may enjoy Your salvation!

20.28.34.en: * My evils have shattered all goodness in me, and their defiled odor has spread within me!

20.28.35.en: I live as in a dream; all the delights my evils offer me pass away; I awake to find myself having gathered wind, and having clung to a shadow and a phantom!

20.28.36.en: My evils take my peace from me, for I have no peace except in Your divine embrace.

20.28.37.en: My evils have corrupted my soul, more than the worms do to my body.

20.28.38.en: * Why do I hoard my evils like a precious treasure, why do I hide them as one who has pity on them?

20.28.39.en: When they are the cause of my eternal destruction?

20.28.40.en: They pour out their poisons in my bowels, and store up for me eternal bitterness!

20.28.41.en: * My evils have become deadly food for me, instead of enjoying the heavenly manna, Your Body and Blood, which grant eternal life.

20.28.42.en: My evils have taken from me the sweetness of the true life.

20.28.43.en: Let me return to You, O Forgiver of sins, and enjoy You, for You are the Life.

20.28.44.en: You bring me back, not to the Garden of Eden nor to the Promised Land, but to the divine embrace.

20.28.45.en: That I may be satisfied with the sweetness of Your love, and rejoice in unity with the heavenly ones!

20.28.46.en: * You are all love. You desire the salvation of all, but it is my evils that condemn me!

20.28.47.en: You are greater than every evil.

20.28.48.en: You grant me Your righteousness, that I may live with You. I live to You and with You.

20.28.49.en: I meet You on the clouds, and enjoy the glory You prepared for me from the foundation of the world.
